required_work: Bind enforcement-coverage evidence to the claim it backs, and refuse an enforcement profile that binds zero declarations.
objective: Close two confirmed gaps in the EnforcementCoverageDeclaration substrate. (a) Evidence: the registered invariants enforce evidence only for the receipted and uncovered states, so a positive mediated claim is satisfied by the declaration's global evidence bag — evidence establishing only discovery passes a mediation requirement, and nothing ties a reference to the claim it is supposed to back. Move evidence into the per-claim shape canon already specifies, or as the cheaper interim register a mediation-evidence invariant alongside the existing two. (b) Binding: node attestation admits a node that declares an enforcement profile while binding an empty declaration-refs list, satisfying the canon binding rule vacuously — and the list is always empty, because the durable evidence family is read-only in practice and the runtime registry has zero callers. Refuse a declared profile that resolves to zero declarations. ENFORCEMENT_COVERAGE_EVIDENCE_AND_BINDING_EXIT=0.
falsifiable_claim: A positive mediated coverage claim is backed by evidence for mediation, and a node that declares an enforcement profile actually binds coverage declarations. Neither holds: a declaration whose only verification evidence proves discovery resolves as fully operable against a mediated requirement, and an admitted node record carries a node_enforcement_profile_ref with an empty enforcement_coverage_declaration_refs list — vacuously satisfying the canon rule that a profile may bind only verified-current declarations.
selected_profile: The selected single-node sovereign-local profile whose node attestation declares an enforcement profile and whose action classes assert coverage states.

canon_snapshot.snapshot_role: Provenance for the canon revision this record was authored against. Drift detection is owned by generated/canon-baseline.v1.json via tools/canon-impact.mjs.

in_scope: Gap (a), per-claim evidence. Canon requires that every positive claim bind a matching mechanism role and verification evidence, and states the shape per fact. The registered invariants file docs/architecture/_meta/schemas/invariants/enforcement-coverage-declaration.v1.invariants.json carries exactly two rules — enforcement_coverage.receipt.evidence.required_when_receipted and enforcement_coverage.gap.required_when_uncovered — and neither covers mediated. Runtime resolution does not close it: crates/services/src/agentic/runtime/enforcement_coverage.rs:521-539 checks that each required claim is true and then checks only that the global /verification/evidence_refs array is non-empty, with receipt evidence required only when the caller asks for it at :540-556. Bind evidence to the claim it backs, by moving evidence into the per-claim shape canon specifies or by registering a mediation-evidence invariant alongside the existing two.

Gap (b), vacuous binding. crates/types/src/app/hypervisoros_node_attestation.rs:788-800 refuses only the reverse direction — declarations without a profile. With a profile ref present and an empty declarations list the loop at :802 never executes and the function returns Ok(vec![]) at :841, yielding an admitted node record at :988-989 whose enforcement_coverage_declaration_refs is empty. The per-declaration checks that do exist are strict and correct — contract validation at :803, foreign-profile refusal at :805-815, verified-current gating at :819-829 — but they never run on an empty list. Refuse a declared node_enforcement_profile_ref that resolves to zero declarations.

Gap (b), why the list is always empty. crates/node/src/bin/hypervisor_daemon_routes/hypervisoros_node_routes.rs:379-398 scans the durable family for node evidence, but that family is only ever read (hypervisoros_node_routes.rs:357 and :386; system_writer_routes.rs:399) — no route in the tree writes a declaration into it. Separately, EnforcementCoverageRegistry has zero callers outside its own module and its store is in-memory by design. A binding rule cannot be satisfied non-vacuously until a producer exists, so the producer is part of this cut's subject even though its shape is owned elsewhere.

Preserve what already works. The overclaiming defenses are real and must survive unchanged: schema rules requiring a mediation-role mechanism, a bounded decision source and final invoker, exclusion of mediated for audit-only and passive operating modes, exclusion under uncovered, and the preventable-implies-mediated rule, all proven to fail closed across the registered negative fixtures.

Keep the canon correction in force. The 2026-07-28 canon pass (commit a5c0f0a59) corrected two false absence claims and recorded both of these gaps honestly in hypervisoros.md and canon-to-code-delta.md: registry residency may be claimed, runtime enforcement may not. This cut closes the gaps; it does not re-open the status question.
out_of_scope: Any widening of what a coverage claim asserts. Discovery still does not imply observation, observation does not imply attribution, attribution does not imply mediation, mediation does not imply prevention, and a receipt still never proves an unobserved external effect.

Declaring runtime enforcement operable. Closing the evidence and binding gaps makes the contract enforceable; it does not make any node's coverage true, and no profile may advertise coverage on the strength of this cut alone.
Rewriting the strict per-declaration checks that already pass, or relaxing any registered negative fixture to accommodate the new rules.
The wider node attestation and re-attestation lifecycle, which has its own owner record.
positive_proof: A positive mediated claim resolves as operable only when evidence bound to mediation is present, and a node declaring an enforcement profile is admitted only when it binds at least one verified-current declaration produced by a real producer path.
adversarial_or_fault_proof: Predeclared branches, each of which must refuse by name: a declaration whose only verification evidence establishes discovery, resolved against a mediated requirement; a declaration with a non-empty global evidence bag but no evidence bound to the claimed state; a mediated claim with a mediation-role mechanism but no mediation evidence; a node record declaring an enforcement profile with an empty declaration-refs list; a node record declaring a profile whose refs resolve to declarations that are not verified-current; a node record binding a declaration belonging to a foreign profile; declarations supplied with no profile ref, which must keep refusing as it does today; a coverage claim advertised while no producer has written a declaration into the durable family; a receipted claim relying on the new mediation rule to skip its own receipt-evidence requirement.

The live defect this cut repairs is retained as its baseline, verified in code at commit 106e2ac797d0949fa463a27680a6255745ea730b and recorded at internal-docs/prompts/architecture-relative-comparison/runs/2026-07-28-leg0-v1-product-truth-verification.md: mediated evidence is unenforced and node binding is satisfiable by binding nothing.

code_anchors.evidence_scope: the resolver whose required-claim loop at :521-539 checks only the global evidence bag, and whose caller-driven receipt-evidence branch sits at :540-556; current behavior is the defect baseline, not proof of this work item

the declaration validator at :788-841 that returns Ok on an empty list and the admitted node record at :988-989 that carries the empty refs; current behavior is the defect baseline, not proof of this work item
the read-only loader at :379-398 over a durable evidence family no route writes; precedent and defect baseline, not proof of this work item

remaining_nonclaims: Closing these gaps makes the contract enforceable. It does not make any deployment's enforcement coverage true, and no profile may advertise or rely on coverage until a producer exists and its declarations resolve as verified-current.
Canon already records both gaps honestly as of the 2026-07-28 correction: registry residency may be claimed, runtime enforcement may not. This record inherits that ceiling and raises it for nothing.
A per-claim evidence binding proves that a reference was declared for the claim, not that the referenced evidence is sufficient. Sufficiency remains an assurance judgment with its own owner.
Refusing an empty declaration list removes a vacuous pass. It creates no obligation that any particular action class be covered, and uncovered remains a legitimate terminal state.
rollback_or_stop_rule: Stop if closing the evidence gap would require weakening any existing structural defense — the mechanism-role requirement, the bounded decision-source and final-invoker enums, the operating-mode exclusions, or the claim-implication rules — because a per-claim evidence rule bought with a weaker overclaiming defense is a net loss of truth. Stop if refusing an empty declaration list would block node admission with no producer available: in that case land the producer first, and record the interim state as an honest known gap rather than admitting nodes vacuously.
exit_criteria: Evidence is bound to the claim it backs for every positive claim state, so a declaration whose evidence establishes only discovery cannot resolve as operable against a mediated requirement.

A declared node enforcement profile that resolves to zero declarations is refused, a producer writes declarations into the durable evidence family, every predeclared adversarial branch refuses by name, every existing negative fixture still fails closed, and the retained literal ENFORCEMENT_COVERAGE_EVIDENCE_AND_BINDING_EXIT=0 appears exactly once.
